signature.name: From screen to doorstep
signature.description: Does the page leave a lost web visitor wanting to walk into the shop, with a concrete reason and enough practical info (when, where) to act on it today?

group-a.signature_why: Live open-now line plus the 9am country loaf gives a real reason to come in, but no address or what's-on-the-counter pull.
group-a.loved: The counter ticket with a bitten loaf as the zero: warm, ownable, and the hours sit above the decoration.
group-a.docked: Hours button jumps to text already on screen; kraft-and-mono reads a touch generic-craft at desktop.

group-b.signature_why: Tells me it's open until 2pm right now, but gives me nothing to go and eat.
group-b.loved: Scoring the visitor's typo onto a loaf is the most surprising idea in the room.
group-b.docked: The loaf is a flat brown ellipse whose score marks read as a frowning face; no 375px check before submitting.

group-c.signature_why: Week grid with today ringed and 'sourdough, a few tables, coffee' lets me plan the visit; no live open-now or address.
group-c.loved: The bake sheet with Monday struck out as 'no bake' feels like the owner's own morning.
group-c.docked: The pencil strike buries the path, and the .html check swaps the real typo for 'this page', so it's illegible either way.
